text.tspan: SQS: visibility timeout, long polling, dead-letter queue
Message visibility timeout (default 30 s, 0 s-12 h)
invisible to other consumers for the visibility timeout
• Not deleted before the timeout ends → visible again → processed TWICE. • Need more time? call ChangeMessageVisibility.
• Timeout too HIGH (hours) and the consumer crashes → re-processing waits a long time. • Too LOW (seconds) → duplicates.
• The 12 h maximum counts from the first receive; extending does not reset it.
• Empty queue? The receive call WAITS for a message
instead of returning empty at once (short polling).
• Fewer API calls, lower cost, lower latency.
• Wait 1-20 s (20 s preferable). Queue level:
• maxReceiveCount = receives allowed before the message
is moved to the DLQ (poison messages).
• Same account, Region and TYPE (FIFO → FIFO DLQ).
• Standard: expiry uses the ORIGINAL enqueue time, so
give the DLQ a longer retention. Redrive moves them back.
Also (docs): delay queues / message timers 0-15 min (default 0) · batches of up to 10 messages for send, receive, delete
• Security: in flight HTTPS · at rest SSE-SQS (SQS-owned keys) or SSE-KMS · client-side encryption if the client encrypts/decrypts itself
• Access: IAM policies for the SQS API · SQS access policies (like S3 bucket policies) for cross-account access and to let SNS, S3... write to the queue
• About 120,000 in-flight (received, not deleted) messages per standard queue
